beliefs: Only the final character of the last whitespace-delimited token is shifted, and only if it is a letter [E1-E15].
A final lowercase letter shifts forward by one in its alphabet, with 'z' wrapping to 'a' [E1, E2, E3].
A final uppercase letter shifts forward by one in its alphabet, with 'Z' wrapping to 'A' [E1, E2, E3].
The shift applies to non-ASCII letters too: accented Latin (é→ê, ñ→ò) and Greek (α→β, Ω→Ϊ) each advance by one code point [E16].
Non-letter final characters (digits, punctuation, whitespace) pass through unchanged [E1-E15].
Empty string maps to empty string [E1].
notes: E16 shows the shift is not limited to ASCII a-z/A-Z; it advances any letter by one code point (é→ê, ñ→ò, α→β, Ω→Ϊ), so I replaced the ASCII-only branches with a general 'letter' check that increments the code point (with ASCII z/Z wrapping).
